plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a two-tier thickness perturbation scheme on a fixed 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 alternating stack can improve dual-band IR filter performance. The hypothesis is that fine-scale phase tuning in the first half of the stack (±3%) combined with envelope adjustment in the second half (±12%) will better separate the two passbands while maintaining stopband suppression. This route uses only recalled knowledge about quarter-wave stack behavior and IR dielectric material pairs - no literature was consulted.

routes.title: Two-tier thickness perturbation on 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 alternating IR filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-tier perturbation scheme with ±3% noise on layers 1-12 and ±12% independent perturbation on layers 13-22 will produce higher target scores than uniform perturbation by decoupling fine-scale phase matching from spectral envelope shaping.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create stopbands through constructive interference of reflections; passbands emerge from defects or envelope modulation. The first half of the stack controls fine interference phase relationships while the second half shapes the broader spectral envelope. Recalled from standard thin-film interference theory.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 layers total, alternating high/low index)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses with two-tier perturbation: layers 1-12 constrained to ±3% around 478.0/815.0 nm baseline, layers 13-22 allowed ±12% independent variation
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
thickness tolerances should reflect the perturbation ranges used in optimization
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness creates maximum reflectance at design wavelength through constructive interference of partial reflections
High/low index contrast (ZnS ~2.3, MgF2 ~1.35 in mid-IR) determines stopband width and reflectance per pair
Dual-passband filters require envelope modulation beyond simple periodic stacks
Front layers dominate fine phase relationships; rear layers influence spectral envelope shape
Recalled from standard thin-film optics design practice, not from checked sources
expected_advantages: Two-tier perturbation may escape local optima that uniform perturbation cannot
Decoupling phase and envelope tuning could better separate the two narrow passbands
Maintains same material pair and layer count as prior iterations for fair comparison
Builds on iteration_08 baseline which achieved 0.698 target score
known_risks: ZnS and MgF2 refractive indices in 4-5 μm range are recalled approximations; actual dispersion data from registry will determine true performance
Daimon-20 substrate index at these wavelengths is recalled as ~1.42 but registry data is authoritative
The 478.0/815.0 nm baseline comes from iteration_08 candidate 1, not from independent quarter-wave calculation at band centers
±3% and ±12% perturbation bounds are heuristic choices; optimal ranges are unknown without literature
22 layers may be insufficient for sharp dual-band separation; 24 layers might perform better but this route fixes 22 for consistency
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer alternating multilayer infrared filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate for dual-band transmission. Stack sequence from air ambient: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (22 layers total). Optimize individual layer thicknesses with two-tier perturbation: layers 1-12 constrained to ±3% variation around baseline thicknesses of 478.0 nm (ZnS) and 815.0 nm (MgF2) alternating; layers 13-22 allowed ±12% independent variation. Spectral range 3500-5300 nm. Target: maximize mean transmittance in passbands 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm; minimize mean transmittance in stopbands 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Normal incidence, coherent thin-film calculation. No metal layers. Materials resolved from registry as zns, mgf2, and CaF2 (Daimon-20).
routes.revision_reason: Refinement per feedback directives: applying two-tier perturbation scheme to layers 1-12 (±3% around iteration_08 candidate 1 baseline) and layers 13-22 (±12% independent) to resolve fine-scale phase mismatches and spectral envelope adjustments while maintaining the same control axis. Repaired material name from ambiguous CaF2 to specific Daimon-20 dataset.

Optimal perturbation percentages for this specific band separation problem
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all iterations of control_route_01 fail to exceed iteration_08's best_target_score of 0.6986 after three refinement rounds, flag this control axis as exhausted and document that the two-tier perturbation hypothesis was not supported for this material system.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase relative to iteration_08's 0.6986 if the two-tier scheme finds better local optima
valid_candidates count should remain similar to prior iterations (around 9) if perturbation bounds are physically reasonable
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly across rounds if the design remains manufacturable
thicknesses_nm for layers 1-12 should cluster near 478.0/815.0 nm baseline with small deviations
thicknesses_nm for layers 13-22 should show wider distribution reflecting the larger perturbation allowance
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce perturbation bounds by half and continue
if tightest_margin becomes negative for all candidates, relax the ±12% bound on layers 13-22 to ±8% and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
